title: Dynamic Provisioning with StorageClasses ⚡
description: Automatically create PVs when PVCs are created.

slides.title: Static vs Dynamic Provisioning ⚖️
slides.content:
# From manual to automatic

**Static**: admin creates PVs manually, users claim them.
**Dynamic**: when a PVC is created, a provisioner (specified in a StorageClass) automatically creates a PV and the backing storage.

Dynamic provisioning is the standard for cloud environments – it’s fast, self‑service, and reduces admin overhead.

slides.title: StorageClass – The Blueprint 📐
slides.content:
## Defines the “class” of storage

```yaml
apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
kind: StorageClass
metadata:
  name: fast-ssd
provisioner: kubernetes.io/aws-ebs
parameters:
  type: gp3
  fsType: ext4
reclaimPolicy: Delete
volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer
```

- `provisioner`: determines which plugin creates the volume (AWS EBS, GCE PD, Azure Disk, NFS, etc.).
- `parameters`: passed to the provisioner.
- `volumeBindingMode`: `Immediate` (default) or `WaitForFirstConsumer` (delays binding until a Pod using the PVC is scheduled – ensures topology awareness).

quizData.question: Which StorageClass parameter controls when the PV is bound?
quizData.explanation: volumeBindingMode can be Immediate (bind on PVC creation) or WaitForFirstConsumer.

slides.title: Using a StorageClass in a PVC 🎯
slides.content:
## Specify the storageClassName

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: PersistentVolumeClaim
metadata:
  name: db-pvc
spec:
  storageClassName: fast-ssd
  accessModes:
    - ReadWriteOnce
  resources:
    requests:
      storage: 20Gi
```

Kubernetes will:
1. Look up the StorageClass `fast-ssd`.
2. Call the provisioner to create an EBS gp3 volume of 20Gi.
3. Create a PV and bind it to this PVC.
4. The Pod can then use the PVC.

slides.title: Create StorageClass and PVC
slides.codeSnippet:
kubectl apply -f storageclass.yaml
kubectl apply -f pvc.yaml
kubectl get pvc db-pvc --watch

slides.title: Default StorageClass ⭐
slides.content:
## One class can be the default

If you mark a StorageClass with `storageclass.kubernetes.io/is-default-class: "true"` annotation, it becomes the default. PVCs that don’t specify `storageClassName` will use it.

Check your cluster’s default:
```bash
kubectl get storageclass
```
The default is marked with `(default)`.

quizData.question: What happens if a PVC has no storageClassName and there is a default StorageClass?

options.text: It uses the default StorageClass for dynamic provisioning
It waits for an admin‑created PV

quizData.explanation: If a default StorageClass exists, it is used automatically.

slides.title: WaitForFirstConsumer 🕒
slides.content:
## Topology‑aware scheduling

With `volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer`, the PV is not created until a Pod that uses the PVC is scheduled. This ensures:
- The volume is created in the same zone as the node.
- No cross‑zone mounting penalties.

Recommended for multi‑zone clusters.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## Expand a PVC online

If the StorageClass has `allowVolumeExpansion: true`, you can resize a PVC by simply increasing its `storage` request. The underlying volume is expanded without downtime (depends on driver support).
